title: Follow-up: AppErrorBoundary fallback heading stays h1 even in fullPage={false} (subtree) mode (PR #84)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #84 (frontend-app-shell-navigation-followups-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step:
PR #84 parameterized AppErrorBoundary's fallback sizing/copy for fullPage=true vs. fullPage=false (subtree) usage, but the fallback heading is still hardcoded to `` (AppErrorBoundary.tsx render()) regardless of `fullPage`. Every page already renders its own `

` via `components/common/PageHeader/PageHeader.tsx` (`component="h1"`). If a future feature wraps just its own subtree with `` inside such a page — the exact scenario this PR and its parent follow-up were built to support — the fallback would render a second `

Something went wrong

` alongside the page's own `

` title, producing an invalid/ambiguous document outline and breaking screen-reader heading navigation. Consider making the heading level conditional on `fullPage` (e.g. `component={fullPage ? 'h1' : 'h2'}`) or otherwise letting a subtree caller override it, so the sizing/copy parameterization this PR added is matched by correct heading semantics too.

decisions.decision: Made the fallback heading's component conditional on fullPage (component={fullPage ? 'h1' : 'h2'}), keeping variant="h4" (visual size) unchanged in both cases, rather than adding a separate headingLevel/component override prop.
decisions.rationale: The task's own description offered this as the preferred option ('e.g. component={fullPage ? 'h1' : 'h2'}'), and the only two real usages are main.tsx (fullPage=true, replacing the whole page — h1 is correct) and a future fullPage=false subtree usage (which needs to sit below a page's own PageHeader h1, so h2 is correct). A caller-supplied override prop would add API surface with no current consumer needing anything other than the fullPage-derived level; can be added later if a real subtree usage needs a different level than h2.
